label: Ropy milk
comment: Soured by the same lactococci as soured milk is, but strains of them that give off slime.

about.text: A Scandinavian type of fermented milk with a stringy, slimy ('ropy') texture. It is soured at room temperature by mesophilic Lactococcus lactis strains that give off exopolysaccharides, long sugar chains that form the slime. The Finnish viili is the best-studied example.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Mesophilic lactococci sour the milk at room temperature while special strains give off slime, long sugar chains that make the gel stringy and 'long'. Diacetylactis strains and Leuconostoc add the buttery aroma.
